highest_value_fixes.fix: Rebuild the interior night value hierarchy: remove the uniform beige veil, retain cool dark structural planes, restrict warm lighting to motivated fixtures, and give trainer/props consistent atmosphere and contact shadows. Fix the blue upper-junction leaks visible in reverse/side nave views.
highest_value_fixes.expected_gain: Architecture, shrine silhouettes and the human should inhabit one lit volume; readable night must retain colour and depth.

highest_value_fixes.fix: Author structural bays and inhabited zones: resolve roof-like interior eaves into believable supported structure, break continuous window repetition, add substantial threshold framing, and group waiting/administrative furnishings into purposeful compositions with clear circulation. Give the end wall a focal use and keep the trainer silhouette clear of its furniture.
highest_value_fixes.expected_gain: A hall with proportion, construction logic and use rather than a huge tiled box. Furniture already helps A, but distribution and hierarchy matter more than more scatter.

highest_value_fixes.fix: Provide distinct shrine pedestals/relic cradles and portal/biome markers with broad recognizable shapes. Current identical lecterns, flat text strips and blank banners cannot communicate sacred objects or destination identity at gameplay size. Use purpose-built meshes/icons/materials consistent with the established stone/timber family.
highest_value_fixes.expected_gain: Clear Hall identity, shrine purpose and navigation without relying on tiny labels.

bar_a_world_fit_rationale: No, for either arm as currently presented. Timber, stone, teal cloth and the blue-clad adventurer are compatible ingredients, and A gives a little of the desired inhabited warmth. The key-art world relies on massing, focal silhouettes, natural palette separation and inviting depth. This hall remains a repetitive box with generic lecterns, large empty planes, weak grounding and a beige night wash. This judgment concerns mood/composition/silhouette, not painted pixel fidelity.
bar_b_atmosphere_rationale: No, for either arm at the requested shipping-quality sense of the question. The third-person adventurer and medieval props suggest the broad genre, but material repetition, incoherent night response, weak contact shadows, roof-junction gaps and insufficient authored focal objects prevent a convincing Palworld/Valheim-class scene. High and Medium were independently inspected; their visible differences are too slight to warrant different scores. No performance inference is made.

palworld_same_kind_of_game_yes_no.qualification: At shipping visual quality; broad third-person fantasy genre cues are present.

overall_verdict: FAIL the scoped authored/coherent/inhabited Hall bar in both arms. A is consistently preferable because benches, the end-wall work area and candles add use and warmth; the gains are modest and do not cure construction, lighting, shrine identity or character-integration defects. Both arms have a coherent basic material family and readable circulation, but neither reaches convincing finished architecture.
character_and_scale: The disclosed fixed idle trainer is judged only as a static visual subject. Blue sleeves, cream collar, brown pack, dark trousers and large hair mass read clearly at 720p, although internal texture detail is coarse and noisy; the face is not shown and cannot be rated. Its stylized proportions suit an adventure game. At the stated 1.80m, doors/ceilings imply an oversized ceremonial volume; this is possible but unsupported spans, immense blank floor and sparse fixtures make the person look miniature. A benches and furniture supply useful human-scale cues. Feet lack a convincing contact shadow, especially at night; this is an apparent grounding defect, not a claim about actual coordinates, animation or collision.
small_size_readability: Sheet-scale trainer and large room outline remain legible. Door text, end-wall props and shrine purposes do not. Night windows and regular floor light blobs dominate while useful furniture and pedestal silhouettes recede. No separate handheld/motion/performance acceptance is claimed.

coverage.references: Keyart and all five supplied Palworld JPGs inspected visually; supplied ART_DIRECTION read for direction.
